newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end lower in a technical selloff.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end lower in a technical selloff.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed lower in technically-driven followthrough selling that is expected to continue through the week, market sources said.
The March contract settled down 1.15 cents to 87.30 cents a lb, traded 89.00 to 86.50 cents. The back months closed 1.30 to 1.05 weaker.
Technical support was seen at 83.80 cents and then at the recent low of 76.40 cents in March. Resistance was pegged at 92.90 and then at the recent high of 99.00 cents.

Fundamentally, expectations for another bout of cold weather in Florida lifted prices earlier this week, but forecasts for temperatures to remain above 40 degrees Fahrenheit later in the week, sparked selling.
Lingering uncertainty over damage from the freeze earlier this month kept prices from falling further.

"No one can quantify what the freeze damage was and what kind of impact we will have," Celeste Georgakis, vice president with Dean Whitter, said. "Because of the uncertainty, we will probably have some choppy days ahead."
Still, Tropicana today said the freeze will lead to a sharp reduction in juice yields per box and the number of fruit to be processed.
Analysts, however, said crop reductions are not likely to move futures prices amid a record U.S. crop, weak demand and additional supplies from Brazil.
The U.S. Department will estimate the damage in its Feb 12 report.
